correctness.rationale: For every gamma≠0 and alpha>gamma²/4, positivity of P and H=y²/2+∫x³/P establish a unique closed oval for each E>0. Original-time quadrature exactly gives f_E and T(E). Changing the two monotone V branches to energy v yields W(v)=c v^{-3/2}+O(v^{-2}), c=1/(sqrt2 alpha^{3/2}), and W(v)=O(v^{-3/4}) at zero. The leading Abel tail integrates exactly to 2c sqrt(1-1/E), so J(E)-C=O(log E/E) after estimating the remainder; C=2pi/sqrt(4alpha-gamma²). Cauchy tail Q=2c/sqrt(E)+O(1/E). An exact signed-density comparison bounds |TV-Q/C| by |J-C|/C, proving the sharp constant and the asymptotically maximizing event. The standard-library quadrature checker passes three finite diagnostics, but the proof does not rely on them.

value.rationale: The published global-center classification leaves quantitative original-time statistics open. A sharp total-variation rate controls all measurable occupation events, not merely weak convergence. Here it identifies a shifted-Cauchy limit, a nontrivial discriminant- and stiffness-dependent first-order coefficient, and the observable event attaining the maximum discrepancy asymptotically. The Abel-tail cancellation also yields a sharper physical-time period estimate. This is a natural uniform-in-energy family theorem over the full open discriminant region, not an arbitrary finite slice.
